product_guards: Require source-bound proposals, complete coherent redirect chains and independent direct HTML 200 observations for the final master. Refuse errors, blocked observations, noindex, conflicting canonicals, loops, external hops, HTTPS downgrades and non-followable statuses.

Support one literal root sitemap in a known static directory and one sibling _redirects file, without a sitemap generator. Re-read current flat rules: every hop, target and status must still match. Reject ambiguous duplicate rules, wildcards, placeholders, conditions, unproved queries, competing Netlify redirects, root .htaccess or Vercel configuration.

A currently resolved static file can shadow a non-forced Netlify rule. Require force for any observed hop with a current source binding. Re-read the final master's unique literal HTML head and reject stale canonicals, noindex, scripts, templates or unreadable sources before any PUT.

Reuse the validated XML byte-offset rewrite from the preceding canonical-sitemap phase. Keep each existing destination's entire entry, remove only the verified old entries, and never transfer alias lastmod/images/priority to a new destination. Minimal creation is tested synthetically, not measured remotely here.

Preserve comments, line endings, significant path case/query/slash, extension data and unrelated entries. Reject malformed XML, DTD, sitemap indexes and ambiguous loc elements. Enforce bounded file size and a readable sitemap blob SHA for the single corrective PUT.

A refused preparation cannot enter heuristic file targeting even if the application helper is called directly. Free-form URL and GitHub preview/confirmation cannot bypass these guards through old cached previews. Individual deep and bulk paths share the deterministic implementation with zero AI billing.

Keep other sitemap families, auditor, catalog, historical receipts and customer sites unchanged. Refused witnesses stay named and detectable; never promote partial cleanup to whole-family or client-readiness certification.

routing_reference.usage: Current file shadowing and force semantics; live controls use 301 and 302 only. Synthetic observation validation also accepts 303, 307 and 308, not a claim that every Netlify rule code or platform is supported.

successful_live_cycle.refusals_explanation: The first redirect ends at an explicitly meta-noindex page. The second ends at a noncanonical page pointing to another master. Neither alias is delisted or claimed repaired.

independent_countercheck.description: Re-read pinned main, seed, baseline and correction branches, both closed draft unmerged PRs and their exact successful builds. Confirm the three setup commits and exactly one corrective commit affecting only sitemap.xml. Independently parse retained entries without inter-entry tails and compare exact full output bytes against removal of three owned fixture blocks. Verify fresh and saved served XML, current native redirect locations/statuses, canonical or refused destination bodies and preview headers, normalizing only the actual owned Netlify deployment-id attribute. Re-prepare the baseline and reproduce the exact rewrite with writes, models, file selection and quota calls forbidden.

acceptance_inventory.after_snapshot: acceptance-after-final.json in the live temporary directory

initial_red.explanation: The broad failure count includes multiple probes of the same unsafe fallback, not 66 independent product bugs.

first_implementation_failure.explanation: A directly called application helper still reached heuristic targeting after refused preparation. Retain an empty guarded redirect plan on refusal so that helper also fails closed; no assertion was weakened.

shadowing_red.explanation: Removing force while a static source exists still allowed a sitemap PUT. Added the current-binding shadow check; this probe now passes without changing its assertion.

limitations: Owned static HTML and flat literal Netlify redirects only, not every customer or stack. Generated, multi-file or ambiguous sitemaps, computed heads, scripts, templates, query conditions, wildcards and other routing formats are conservatively refused. This narrows safe execution, not universal advertised coverage.

Raw previews keep their noindex header and canonical-host alias context. Their sitemap serves production-host URLs with zero crawl seeds; raw family counts are 0 before and after and cannot establish repair. The existing exact preview-host/header projection with saved served XML measures 5 to 2, not production indexation. Fresh HTTP and exact XML checks independently prove the bounded change.

Two redirects remain listed because their final destinations are unsuitable. Existing masters only are measured remotely; minimal creation and complex metadata are tested synthetically. Navigation deliberately preserves all five redirect witnesses after delisting, so a vanished observation cannot create a false success.

The branch config, current master head and sitemap SHA are re-read, but later server-side routing, headers or external customer state may change. This is not a live production transaction or a guarantee against all deployment drift or network failures.

No production recovery replay, receipt migration, agent deployment, customer onboarding, scheduler/payment workflow, capacity test or fresh PostgreSQL run is included. SQLite retains its existing skipped tests, and no all-green or client-readiness verdict is claimed.
next_acceptance_check: Validate noindex pages listed in a sitemap on an owned rebuilt fixture with preserved indexable masters and explicit negative controls, then other offered families and client onboarding.
